body: @QbieShay I've submitted a potential fix. This is uncharted territory for me so let me know of any further issue. I am sourcing a blog post and the original Call of duty slideshow for the implementation instead, so it's slightly different.

While parameters `intensity` and `velocity_multipliers` allow `or_greater`, but they are restricted by this clamping, making the effect almost not works. You will likely need to consider increasing the tile size or separating the blurring process from the tile size.
Motion blur does not work when the scaling mode is set to `FSR2.2`. I assume `MetalFX Temporal` probably does not work either by similar reason.

When changing `intensity` from `0` to `0.01`, a sudden hitch sometimes occurs. Also, isn't it likely that out of sync could occur in the `num_camera_attributes_with_motion_blur` when the `intensity` is `0`?

Also, there is an issue where the intensity of the blur depends on the FPS, but this issue may be hidden by the https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115027/changes#r4053094717 clamping issue. Currently, `p_time_step` looks a dead argument. Intensity `0.1`: FPS 144: FPS 10:

Thank you for pointing out that `velocity_multipliers` allow `or_greater`, only `intensity` should allow `or_greater` so I will fix that.
As for the clamping, you are correct to point out the obvious limitation it imposes, however there's not much that can be done. The clamping is necessary for visual robustness in the face of the limited tile size. As long as velocities don't saturate the clamp, `intensity` and `velocity_multipliers` work as expected.
I tried clamping before applying the intensity and multipliers, which either reveal the ugly seams between tiles again or throw the blending off due to the same velocity being used differently between the foreground, midground and background samplings.

This is expected. The intensity is a multiplier to the otherwise-natural blur that occures between frames. It's equivalent to the shutter angle of real cameras. This means it scales the already existing motion vectors, and those are based on screen UV difference from the last frame. The higher the framerate, the smaller the positional change, the less blur you need.

Now, the reason absolutely no blur occures on the 144 fps example, is because of the velocity thresholds, which are now by default set to non-0 values. These filter out velocities below some threshold, you can read more about them here:
https://github.com/sphynx-owner/Godot-Motion-Blur-Addon#velocity-thresholds

We've decided to apply non-0 velocity thresholds, as well as a default multiplier of 0.1 for camera rotation velocities, over on the discord workgroup chat. Our aim is to give default values that would make the motion blur a tasteful, viable addition to games where otherwise users would feel awful nausea or discomfort.
Thank you for pointing this out. I will figure this out.
Yeah, I think I am stupid and I needed to put the condition in brackets, sorry for the clumsiness.

I assume there are likely a fair number of users who perceive the heavy blurring that occurs when lag happens as a bug, so if the fps normalization feature is to be removed, you must provide documentation that is clear to everyone. If not, we’ll end up repeatedly responding to issue reports submitted by users who perceive this as a bug by saying, "This is intended behavior as motion-blur author said".

But if possible, I believe the ideal solution would be to make normalization based on the FPS delta time optional as salvaging the dead argument.

I hope this would not be necessary. Adding something like this would go against why we removed the framerate modes in the first place, introducing similar complexity under a different hat. The reason I felt it was ok to remove them was because the tile-clamping could be in charge of taming the velocities, so even at high lag you would have an acceptable experience. I believe this is a satisfactory solution.

In that case, you must remove the dead arguments and add documentation.

Also, we will likely need opinions from other contributors. Personally, I vote against that remove fps normalization (although, it isn't huge blocker). Then, we should ask the rendering team and other contributors; if a majority of them are in favor, then I think it would be acceptable.

The removal was requested by @QbieShay. I will get rid of the dead arguments, thanks for pointing those out. I think for simplicity's sake this is a fair change, reducing redundancy and complexity. How should I update the documentation in this case? do you mean inside the code or in the docs?
If documenting, I think the two appropriate places would be "description" and "member intensity" in the class reference.

In addition, I recommend including a note in the clamping code section explaining the side effects of removing the clamp. Specifically, a comment such as, "Since the current motion blur depends on the FPS, the clamp prevents large blur from occurring in the FPS dropping".

That is one of the reason why oppose removing FPS normalizing. They should be architecturally independent and not dependent on one another. For example, if a PR is merged that allows for adjusting the clamp when a better processing method is found in the future, we might end up receiving reports that the blurring during FPS drops has become worse.

> Also, we will likely need opinions from other contributors. Personally, I vote against that remove fps normalization (although, it isn't huge blocker). Then, we should ask the rendering team and other contributors; if a majority of them are in favor, then I think it would be acceptable.

@TokageItLab  I want first and foremost to reduce the API surface for now, and in a way that's forward compatible. If there's actual user demand, we'll expose more parameters, but we should start with a minimal set and only expose what's necessary.

I have done the same for trail3D, and I believe this is a winning strategy for us: it avoid speculative features ("what if users want this") and focuses on providing a good solution without too much complexity both for users and for us.

So the focus for this should be "how do we keep this forward compatible if one day we want to expose those parameters"

@TokageItLab, @QbieShay helped me realize an error in my implementation so far. While the blurring itself should stay framerate-dependent (you want the blur to fill in the gaps between frames), the velocity thresholds should be framerate independent, meaning the blur would activate more predictably regardless of framerate.

The purpose of the velocity thresholds is to be sensible of human's eye tracking capabilties, leaving trackable features crisp. This is based on the visual speed of the object across the screen and is not dependent on the framerate in any way.
I am sorry for not having realized this earlier, would have saved us a lot of headache.
